claims.claim: For w=(2,7,4,8,1,6,3,5), complete rook placements correspond bijectively to perfect matchings between 14 across words and 14 down words.
claims.evidence: Each orientation has six lines with two nonempty words and two lines with one, totaling 14. Every white cell belongs to exactly one word of each orientation, and each across/down pair intersects in at most one cell. Consequently cell selection and edge selection give mutually inverse maps between complete placements and perfect matchings.
claims.witness: The omitted empty words are R4, L5, U2, and D5. Scanning the grid produces 14 across words, 14 down words, and 56 white cells.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed maximal white segments directly from the black cells; checked both word partitions and every across/down intersection.

claims.claim: Every complete placement for this permutation contains (1,1), (2,8), (8,3), (1,7), and (2,4).
claims.evidence: L1, R2, D3, and U7 are the singleton words containing the first four cells. U4 consists of (1,4) and (2,4). Since forced cell (1,7) occupies R1, (1,4) is forbidden, forcing (2,4). Exhaustive cell-level enumeration independently confirms that all five occur in every placement.
claims.witness: Each listed cell occurs in all 155 placements. Their matching edges are L1–U1, R2–U8, L8–D3, R1–U7, and L2–U4.
claims.search_method: Checked singleton propagation, enumerated every complete placement, and independently computed zero perfect matchings after deleting each forced edge individually.

claims.claim: Deleting the five forced matching edges and their incident words leaves a nine-by-nine incidence graph with the neighborhoods listed below, without changing the number of complete placements.
claims.evidence: The five edges have distinct endpoints in both parts, leaving nine words per part. Direct intersections reproduce every listed neighborhood. Restriction removes the forced edges from any original matching; adjoining them extends any residual matching uniquely, proving preservation of the count.
claims.search_method: Rebuilt words independently as coordinate intervals, checked endpoint deletion and all neighborhoods, enumerated all 362880 residual bijections, and validated every matching's extension against the original words.

claims.claim: Define T(p,q) as the number of matchings of rows B,C,D,E,H onto columns {p,4,5,6,q}. The desired count is the sum, over p=1,2,3, of 2T(p,7)+T(p,8)+T(p,9).
claims.evidence: The only assignments (A,G) are (2,1), (3,1), and (3,2), leaving each p once. The only assignments (F,I) are (8,9), (9,8), (9,7), and (8,7), leaving q=7 twice and q=8,9 once each. These assignments use disjoint row and column sets. Each remaining completion is precisely one matching counted by T(p,q), giving a disjoint exhaustive decomposition.
claims.witness: The multiplicities are p:(1,1,1) and q:(2,1,1). Actual residual matching counts grouped by p and q are [[8,14,7],[20,28,15],[20,28,15]].
claims.search_method: Exhaustively enumerated the conditioning assignments and grouped all residual perfect matchings by their unused p and q; checked each group against its multiplicity times T(p,q).

claims.evidence: Restricted to rows B,C,D,E,H, both columns 2 and 3 have neighborhood {C,D,E}. Replacing column 2 by column 3 in a matching preserves every incidence and has the inverse replacement, proving the equality for each stated q.
claims.witness: Both rows of the minor table are (10,28,15), for q=(7,8,9).
claims.search_method: Checked neighborhood equality and verified that column replacement maps each exhaustively enumerated matching set bijectively onto the other.

claims.evidence: Column 1 forces E→1 and column 7 forces H→7. B can use 5 or 6; for either choice, C and D can take the remaining two columns in either order. Thus T(1,7)=2·2=4.
claims.witness: In row order (B,C,D,E,H), the four assignments are (5,4,6,1,7), (5,6,4,1,7), (6,4,5,1,7), and (6,5,4,1,7).
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 120 column permutations of the minor and checked the two B branches separately.

claims.evidence: E→1 is forced. On columns {4,5,6,8}, rows B,C,D,H permit every edge except B→4 and H→6. Inclusion–exclusion therefore gives 4!−3!−3!+2!=14.
claims.witness: The two forbidden-edge events have sizes 6 and 6, with intersection size 2; 24−6−6+2=14.
claims.search_method: Checked the permitted edges and enumerated all 120 column permutations of the five-row minor using exact integers.

claims.evidence: E→1 is forced, and only D or H can occupy column 9. H→9 leaves four assignments of B,C,D. With D→9, B→5 leaves one assignment and B→6 leaves two. These cases are disjoint and exhaustive, giving 4+1+2=7.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 120 column permutations and verified the exhaustive branch partition.

claims.evidence: H→7 is forced. B→5 leaves E two choices, each allowing two orders for C,D. B→6 leaves E three choices, each again allowing two orders. B has no other permitted column, so the total is 4+6=10.
claims.witness: The B→5 and B→6 branches contain 4 and 6 matchings respectively.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 120 column permutations and counted both B branches exactly.

claims.evidence: C and D allow all five columns. B,E,H have allowed sets {5,6,8}, {2,4,5}, and {4,5,8}. Choosing B=5,6,8 leaves respectively 3,7,4 distinct-column assignments for E,H. Each permits two orders for C,D, giving 2(3+7+4)=28.
claims.witness: Complete matching counts for B=5,6,8 are respectively 6,14,8.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 120 column permutations and checked the three conditioning counts and remaining two-row multiplicity.

claims.evidence: Only D or H can occupy column 9. H→9 leaves the same four-row problem as T(2,7), contributing ten. With D→9, B→5 forces C→6,E→2,H→4; B→6 allows H=4 or 5 and two orders for C,E in each case. Thus the total is 10+1+4=15.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 120 column permutations and verified the exhaustive branch partition.

claims.claim: The recorded equivalence is false: |RP(Grid(2,7,4,8,1,6,3,5))|=155, although 155≡3 modulo 4.
claims.evidence: The proved decomposition gives (2·4+14+7)+2(2·10+28+15)=155. Independent exhaustive cell selection, full-graph permanent calculations, and residual enumeration agree. The tuple is a permutation in S8, and 155=4·38+3, so this realized positive count violates the proposed necessary condition.
claims.search_method: Counted placements directly from maximal white segments, cross-checked by exact subset dynamic programming and integer inclusion–exclusion, and independently verified the complete minor certificate.

target_evidence: The exact target expressly permits either proving the spectrum equivalence or rigorously disproving it. Independently reconstructing the grid under the supplied maximal-white-segment definition establishes exactly 155 complete placements for w=(2,7,4,8,1,6,3,5). Thus the existential side holds for r=155 while the proposed arithmetic condition fails because 155≡3 modulo 4. This concrete counterexample fully satisfies the disproof alternative. The draft's FULL claim and final conclusion are therefore accurate; a replacement classification is not required by the target.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and baseline draft as source material; used no web, retrieval database, prior verification report, or other solution.
Judged coverage against the exact target's explicit disproof alternative independently of claimed_resolution and self_assessment.
